confirmed.title: Kept end cells shield a trench vertex, so the kept water and the first piece end up separated (by a 2.5 m hole before bury, a dry lip after)
confirmed.scenario: kit-118 upstream end, the one fix (1) targets. The first piece is dropped at the platform, so A[0] sits at (556.55, 1377.80), i_first=20 and keep_v = (558,1377) and (558,1378) (bq 9.92 and 8.75). kd (line 285) keeps every cell that touches a kept vertex, and KEEP_Q (4.5 m) is smaller than one cell (6 m). The kept cells (557,1377) and (557,1378) therefore include corner (557,1378). That vertex is a non-kept body vertex: near=16 < i_first, bq=2.93 <= KEEP_Q, q=2.93 <= TRENCH. Because its cells stay in env, it lands in `protect`, then in `fz` (lines 299-301), so the trench skips it (line 304, `& ~fz`) and fill_pits treats it as a drain (line 343). It stays at H0 4.55, which is 2.11 m below the roadway (6.67) and 2.77 m below its trench seat (7.33). Meanwhile its other cells, (556,1377) and (556,1378), touch `rest`, so they are cut (lines 286-291). That makes (557,1378) a submerged border of the kept water: a new exposed water edge over a hole. In terrain-kit.npz the first piece's upstream sheet end also hangs up to 1.54 m above the terrain (v5: 0.42 m). Only the separate bury pass hides this, by raising (557,1378) +2.53 m to 7.09 (max kept plane 7.03 + 0.06). That height is above the kit sheet (6.92) and above the kept planes at that vertex (6.98 and 7.03). In the final terrain the kept pond (rows 557-558, z 8928-8940) and the first piece's sheet (which starts at z 8940.8-8945.0) are separated by a dry strip 0.8-5 m wide. So the docstring claim that trimmed ends 'stay wet and connected' and that 'the kit covers the rest' does not hold. The pattern follows from the code, not from this site: the first wet non-kept vertex on the kd boundary always keeps a cut cell (bcell includes every cell touching `rest`), so it is always a submerged footprint border. Being protected, neither the trench nor the pit fill can fix it.
confirmed.verdict:
The defect is real. I reproduced it by rerunning v6 into scratch with an instrumented copy (patched only to dump per-site state). The rerun matches the published outputs exactly: heights equal terrain-kit.npz (np.array_equal), and cover and envelope equal cover-ev108.npy and envelope-ev108.npy (equal_nan).

What the kit-118 dump shows:
- i_first=20, i_last=581, and keep_v is [(558,1377), (558,1378)].
- Line 285 (kd) keeps cells (557,1377) and (557,1378). Their corner (557,1378) is a non-kept body vertex: near=16, bq=2.93, q=2.93, which is inside TRENCH.
- Those kept cells stay in env (planes 7.15/7.03/6.98, plus 7.12/7.10 in row 558), so the vertex becomes protect and therefore fz (lines 299-301). The trench skips it (line 304, `& ~fz`) and fill_pits treats it as a drain (line 343).
- It stays at its H0 of 4.55. The roadway yq there is 6.67 and its trench seat seat_v is 7.33.
- It is the only protected vertex with q <= TRENCH. The report count frozen_or_protected_in_trench goes from 0 (v5) to 1 (v6).
- The cells to its north, (556,1377) and (556,1378), are cut (env is NaN there). So the pre-bury kit terrain has a dry cell whose corner sits 2.5 m below the kept water next to it.

Sheet check, using piece 0's matrix from kit-records.json and the native-split interpolator:
- The highest point of the upstream sheet edge above the terrain is 1.54 m in terrain-kit (the checker gives 0.42 m for v5). Along the axis the kit terrain is 5.6-5.98 m under a sheet at 6.90-6.98 m.
- The bury pass changes only this vertex: bury-report.json pass 0 new = [[8268, 8940]], changed_vs_input 1 (v5: none, 0). It raises the vertex to 7.09 m.
- In terrain-ev108.npz the terrain along the axis from the sheet end (z=6) to 4.5 m upstream is 7.12-7.44 m. That is above the sheet (6.92-6.98) and above the kept pond planes (6.98-7.15), so there is a dry strip between the kept pond and the first piece. The sheet's last ~0.5 m is buried (final terrain 7.00-7.12 against a sheet at 6.91-6.92).
- At the chord end A[0], the final terrain (7.12) is also above the roadway minus AXIS_CLEAR (6.64).

The mechanism comes from the code, not from this site. KEEP_Q (4.5 m) is smaller than one cell (6 m), so kd keeps whole cells whose other corners lie inside the trench radius. Fix (1)'s claim that trimmed ends 'stay wet and connected' therefore fails at kit-118 upstream, the very case it targets. The v5 plug itself is gone: (558,1377..1379) stay at 5.55/6.41/8.21.

The defect is in both EV108 v6 outputs: terrain-kit.npz has the hole, and terrain-ev108.npz has the bury-raised lip and the dry gap. In the env/cover cut (:291) it excludes those cells. Cells (557,1377) and (557,1378) keep their planes, 7.03 and 6.98, and (557,1376) keeps 7.15 (envelope-ev108.npy). confirmed.title: fill_pits fills the trench basins of earlier sites: drains include only this site's trench, while fillable includes every vertex an earlier site changed
confirmed.scenario: The drains are trench | axis_moved | fz for the current site only (line 343). fillable includes (h != h0), and h0 = H0[sub] is the original terrain (line 301), so every vertex an earlier site carved inside this window is fillable at any q (line 345). trench_all is built (line 349) but never used as a drain. A kit trench is usually a closed basin, because the roadway falls downstream and the end meets a bank or a protected rim, as at kit-118's outlet (trench 1.48 m against a protected bank at 2.9 m). Any later site whose bounding window covers it fills it to its spill level. The window is the chain bbox +-20 m plus the body +-4 vertices, and kit-7's window is already 174x147 vertices. The earlier site's report was written before the later site ran, so it still says axis_unresolved=0. v5 could only touch earlier work within OUTER=14 m (outer raise), while the v6 fill reaches the whole bbox. The pilot is not affected because the two windows are disjoint (kit-118 rows 508-562 cols 1365-1384, kit-7 rows 21-194 cols 1382-1528). A multi-site run where a tributary and the stream it joins are both kitted would hit it.
confirmed.verdict:
The defect is real: I reproduced it with the unchanged code, and a one-line drain fix makes it go away. It does not affect the EV108 v6 output.

Code reading of tools/water/streambed_kit_v31.py:
- Line 343 builds the drains from this site's own trench | axis_moved | fz, plus the window border at line 344.
- Line 345 makes every vertex with h != h0 fillable. h0 is H0[sub], the original terrain (line 301), so every vertex an earlier site carved inside this window is fillable at any q.
- trench_all collects earlier trenches at line 349, but the fill never uses it. The only other reader is the slope guard (line 380).
- fz (frozen | protect, line 301) does not cover an earlier trench: that site's pond cut set its envelope cells to NaN, so they are no longer protected.
- fill_pits (lines 128-143) therefore raises a closed earlier trench to the level where it spills into the later window's border or drains.

Independent reproduction in my own scratch folder refute_fill343:
- I used the checker's syn_two.py only to generate the synthetic inputs (site A is a tributary with a closed downstream end, site B is an L-shaped stream processed after it).
- I ran the real v6 file unchanged; it is identical to the checker's kit_v6.py copy.
- I measured A's own pieces from kit-records.json: water-face samples every 0.5 m along each piece's z, compared with roadway-0.03 on the native triangulation.
- A alone: 0 of 407 samples have terrain above that level. Column 1000, rows 1010-1040, runs 6.97 down to 5.66.
- A then B: 275 of 407 samples are above, by up to 1.26 m. Column 1000, rows 1010-1040, is flat at 7.16. B's report shows pits_filled=35 and pit_fill_max_m=1.59.
- A's report still says axis_unresolved=0 and pits_filled=0, because it is written before B runs.
- Patched copy with drain = trench | axis_moved | fz | trench_all[sub]: 0 of 407 samples above, column 1000 is identical to the A-alone run, and B's pits_filled drops to 1. So the line 343/345 fill is the cause, not B's trench or outer raise.

EV108 v6: sites.json has only kit-118 then kit-7. In ev108-kit/terrain-kit.npz the changed vertices (v31_kit) form two separate clusters: rows 23-191 / cols 1384-1525 (kit-7) and rows 512-556 / cols 1369-1381 (kit-118). kit-7's window extends only a few vertices beyond its changes (about rows 21-194), so it cannot reach kit-118's trench. The defect would only show in a run where two kitted sites have overlapping windows, such as a tributary and the stream it joins.

confirmed.title: Fix (6) is incomplete: axis samples are not clamped, so a stream at the S/E edge crashes and one at the N/W edge wraps to the opposite side of the window
confirmed.scenario: The window is clamped to rows and cols [1, 2046] (lines 260-261). The axis samples (lines 323-328) still use int(r_), int(c_), ri+1 and ci+1 against that window, and the last piece may overrun the end by 6 m. If a chain reaches row or col 2046 (stream within about 12 m of the south or east edge), ri+1-r0 indexes past the window and line 332 raises IndexError. If a chain reaches row or col < 1 (north or west edge, or the overrun past it), ri-r0 is -1 or -2. That index wraps to the last rows of the window, so the axis fix lowers unrelated vertices on the far side of the window, and they become drains, so the fill keeps the holes. Nothing is reported (axis_unresolved stays 0). Separately, geodesic (line 86) still does body[b] with b=2048 when a body touches row or col 2047 (an existing crash the fix does not cover).
confirmed.verdict:
Confirmed from the code, without running the full script. In v6 the window is clamped to [1, 2046] at tools/water/streambed_kit_v31.py:260-261. The edited arrays h and fz have the window's shape, (r1-r0+1, c1-c0+1). The axis samples at lines 322-328 do not clamp ri = int(r_) or ci = int(c_), and they index ri+1 and ci+1. They store window indices rr-r0 and cc-c0, and lines 332/335/344 use those directly.

South/east edge: when a chain sample reaches row or col 2046, ri+1 = 2047, so the index is r1+1-r0, one past the window. That raises IndexError at line 332. This happens when r1 is clamped to 2046.

North/west edge: int() truncates toward zero. A sample with r_ in (-1, 1) gives ri = 0, and with r0 clamped to 1 the index is -1. A sample further out gives -2. NumPy wraps these negative indices to the far side of the window, so the axis fix lowers unrelated vertices. Those vertices are marked axis_moved, so they become drains at line 346 and the pit fill leaves them alone. axis_unresolved at line 343 reads through the same wrapped indices, so it still reports 0.

geodesic at line 86 also reads body[b] without a bounds check. A body touching row or col 2047 raises IndexError there. That crash already existed and fix (6) did not add a check for it.

Fix (6) is therefore incomplete as claimed: the clamps cover only tri_h (line 118), piece_blocked (line 222) and the window itself.

EV108 v6 is not affected. sites.json has only kit-118 (seed 8235, 9125) and kit-7 (seed 8688, 11478). I took the T column of every matrix in kit-records.json (185 records). Rows run from about 25.9 to 555.6 and cols from about 1370 to 1523. So the windows are far from rows and cols 0-1 and 2046-2047: no negative or overflowing index happens, and these branches never run. The defect is real but latent, and only shows for streams within about 12 m of the map border.

confirmed.title: Fix (1) side effect: a kept-water cell protects a vertex inside the first piece's trench, leaving a 2.1 m hole that the bury pass then seals
confirmed.scenario: kit-118 upstream. keep_v keeps vertices (558,1377) and (558,1378) because they are more than KEEP_Q from the chain. kd (line 285) spares the six cells around them from the cut. Lines 299-301 then protect all four corners of those cells. One corner, (557,1378), sits at q=2.93 m, inside TRENCH of piece 0 (A0 = row 556.55, col 1377.8), and gets weight 0.55 at the first axis sample. Since it is protected it stays at H0 4.55 m. confirmed.verdict:
I tried to refute this and could not; the defect holds. To check it I ran an instrumented copy of the v6 script in scratch on the EV108 inputs. Its outputs match the published ones: cover-ev108.npy, envelope-ev108.npy, kit-records.json and kit-report.json have identical sha256, and the heights in terrain-kit.npz are equal. The instrumented run printed the following for kit-118.

Line 284 sets keep_v to {(558,1377), (558,1378)}. Line 286 (kd) keeps the envelope and cover cells around those two vertices out of the cut. Lines 299-300 then protect every corner of the remaining envelope cells, and line 301 puts those corners in fz. One of those corners is vertex (557,1378). Its values there:
- q = 2.926, which is inside TRENCH = 3.0
- protect and fz are True, and trench is False (because of the ~fz at line 304)
- it is a drain, so the pit fill does not raise it
- h stays at H0 = 4.554 m, while seat_v = 7.327 and yq = 6.669

A0 lies at row 556.55, col 1377.80. The first axis sample's triangle is (556,1377) w0.199, (556,1378) w0.247 and (557,1378) w0.555. Because fz stops the axis fix from moving this vertex (line 334), the surface under piece 0's upstream end sits 0.9 m below the roadway in terrain-kit.npz (5.78 against 6.67). v5 had this vertex at 6.64.

The published outputs show the consequences:
- kit-report frozen_or_protected_in_trench goes from 0 in v5 to 1 in v6.
- envelope-ev108 and cover-ev108 keep cells (557,1376..1378) at 7.15 / 7.02 / 6.98 and (558,1376..1378); v5 had removed them.
- bury-report.json in v6 has one new exposed point, [8268, 8940], which is exactly vertex (557,1378); v5 had none.
- terrain-ev108.npz raises that vertex to 7.085, above the kept planes 6.98 and 7.025. The water fix (1) kept is closed off again at that corner.

The effect on the final terrain is worse than the checker says. With the bury pass's 7.085, the surface along the first ~1.5 m of piece 0's axis is 7.18 / 7.05 / 6.93 / 6.81, against a roadway of 6.67 / 6.66 / 6.65 / 6.65. The terrain pokes up to about 0.5 m through the plate's upstream end. In the kit stage, before the bury pass, it was a 0.9 m hole instead.

Root cause: the protection from kd plus protect covers corners of kept cells that lie within TRENCH of the chain. This is a new defect from the v6 fix (1). It reaches the final EV108 v6 terrain.

confirmed.title: Fix (5) incomplete: the whole excess still lands on a low-weight wall vertex, which drops to the target (v5 behaviour)
confirmed.scenario: A sample's heavy trench vertices already sit at the target, because an earlier sample floored them there. `h[rr, cc] > top` drops them from mv. That leaves only the far vertex, with weight around 0.01, as movable. h - e/sw then lowers it by e/w (metres) and the floor stops it at the target. Result: terrain 5-6 m from the axis ends up at roadway-0.03, under the visible sheet, which is the round-1 defect (5) widening.
confirmed.verdict:
The claim holds. I reproduced it with an instrumented copy of v6, kept in my scratch folder (scratchpad/refute_ax334/kit_instr.py). The only change is a log line inside the axis loop. I ran it on the EV108 inputs, and its heights are equal to ev108-kit/terrain-kit.npz (np.array_equal True, max diff 0.0).

Code (tools/water/streambed_kit_v31.py:334-337): mv keeps only vertices with h > top. The floor max(top, h - e/sw) means no vertex can go below the target. So once the heavy trench vertices of a crossed triangle sit at the target, the light third vertex is the only one left that can move, and the floor sends it straight down to the target. That is the v5 behaviour that round 1 flagged as widening.

Log, kit-7, pass 0, sample 2611: top 1.5713 (roadway 1.6013 minus 0.03), e 0.0533. Vertices (153,1489) and (154,1489) had already been floored to exactly 1.5713 by samples 2609 and 2593 (same top, because the roadway is flat here), so they were left out of mv. (154,1490) has w 0.01235 = sw and q 5.07 m. It goes from 5.887 to 1.5713, a 4.3 m cut to clear 5 cm.

Over kit-7, 28 vertices were lowered more than 0.3 m only by samples where their weight was below 0.05: 37.5 m of cut in total. 23 of them have q > 2.75 and end under the sheet level yq+0.25 (for example (172,1506) q 5.45, 5.00 to 1.56; (179,1501) q 6.00, 3.91 to 1.56). All 28 have the same height in v6 and v5 (within 0.02 m), both in terrain-kit.npz and in the final terrain-ev108.npz. Pit fill and the slope guard do not raise them back, because axis_moved vertices are drains and are excluded from the slope guard's movable set. kit-118 has no such cases.

A better solution existed in this case: lowering the trench vertices about 5 cm below top would clear the sample, since the trench seat at q=0 is already roadway-0.33. The floor rules that out.

Not checked: the checker's global 135 vs 210 widening count, and a visual check in the client.

confirmed.title: Fix (3) skip is unreachable for the only pre-trim empty-chain case: a single-vertex body still crashes at line 183

The run aborts with no outputs.
confirmed.verdict:
I could not refute it. The single-vertex crash is real and reproduces. It is narrow and it already existed in v5; v6 did not introduce it.

How I checked it (scratch script, read-only, gis-env python -I, importing tools/water/streambed_kit_v31.py and rebuilding vp/wet/lab exactly as main() does at lines 149-158 from terrain-ev107.npz and fp-ev107/footprint.npz):
- Seed [9162,10374] maps to (318,1527). That vertex is wet, its label body has size 1, and it is the only wet vertex in the 7x7 window, so the assert at line 166 passes.
- path_between gives path [(318,1527)]. smooth() returns it unchanged. resample() (lines 101-104) returns P with shape (1,2) and s=[0.0].
- np.gradient(P, axis=0) then raises ValueError 'Shape of array too small to calculate a numerical gradient'. That call is line 183, which runs before the chain loop and before the new `if not chain:` skip at lines 233-235. The run aborts.

The checker's reasoning also holds:
- A body with 2 or more vertices has distinct geodesic ends at least 6 m apart. smooth() keeps the ends fixed, so s[-1] >= 6 and the loop at lines 191-194 always adds at least one piece.
- So a chain can only be empty before trimming for a single-vertex body, and that case dies at line 183 first. The new skip is only reached when trimming empties the chain, and that case works.
- The input has 143 single-vertex wet bodies in total.

Scope and severity:
- The same code (resample, then np.gradient) is in v5, so this is a crash that fix (3) does not cover, not one v6 introduced.
- It is a crash with no outputs, not a corruption, and it only happens if sites.json seeds an isolated wet vertex.

Effect on EV108 v6: none. sites.json holds only kit-118 and kit-7, both multi-vertex bodies that produced chains, and the v6 outputs exist (terrain-kit.npz, terrain-ev108.npz, kit-records.json, kit-report.json).

I did not run the full kit with the iso-1 site. I reproduced the exact code path up to line 183 instead.

rejected.title: Shared RNG makes kit-7 records change although its chain is unchanged (v6 extra kit-118 stones reshuffle variants and stone models)
rejected.reason:
The checker's observation is accurate, but it is not a defect in the sense this review asks for. It is not a fix that fails, and v6 did not introduce it.

What holds up:
- One generator, `rng = np.random.default_rng(20261013)`, is shared by all sites (streambed_kit_v31.py:159).
- That generator is drawn once per long piece at :237 and twice per stone at :359.
- sites.json processes kit-118 before kit-7.
- Comparing v5-run/kit-records.json with kit-records.json reproduces the claim: 11 of kit-7's non-stone pieces swap between `long_straight` and `long_straight_2` (for example pieces 2, 8 and 20). kit-7 goes from 155 to 158 records.

Why it is not a defect:
1. It is not new in v6. v5 has the same shared generator (kit_v5_for_review.py:128) with the same draws (:203, :301). Any change to an earlier site's number of long pieces or stones already reshuffled later sites in v5. v6 only exercises the existing coupling.
2. It does not touch terrain or water. The variant is picked at :237-238, after the chain has been built and trimmed. The chain and its A/B/ya/yb values, which drive the terrain cut, never read the variant. The variant is used in only two places:
   - the model name (:249);
   - `T = M - R @ [0, ROAD[kind], 0]` (:248). This shifts the placement origin by exactly the 0.04 m ROAD difference, so both variants put the roadway at the same world height. That is the 0.0400 maxdiff the checker saw: a compensating offset, not a misplacement.
3. What remains is cosmetic: which of two valid vanilla 24 m pieces is placed, and each stone's model and yaw. Output is still deterministic for a given sites.json. A per-site seed would make v5/v6 visual comparisons cleaner, but that is a reproducibility nicety. No piece or water face is wrong and no terrain changes.

Effect on EV108 v6: kit-7's records differ from v5 only in variant and stone choice. Terrain, cover, envelope and roadway heights are unaffected.
